newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. athletes charged in bomb-making prank. [CORRECTED 2:33 GMT 18/10]
newsitem.headline: N.Y. athletes charged in bomb-making prank. [CORRECTED 2:33 GMT 18/10]

text.p: Eight high school students were arrested for allegedly making bombs and planting them at the homes of fellow students to celebate their football team's victory over a rival school, authorities said Thursday.
None of the bombs exploded, said the Montgomery County, New York, sheriff's office.
"They were celebrating," said Sheriff Investigator Bill Gilston. "They were blowing off steam the wrong way."

The eight -- all members of the Fonda-Fultonville High School football team -- face felony weapons possession charges. A ninth suspect, a college student in Buffalo, New York, was expected to be arrested this weekend, authorities said.
The students allegedly planted 12 homemade bombs last weekend, after their team won a Saturday game against Albany Academy, on the driveways and lawns of fellow students and football players.
The bombs were made with toilet bowl cleaner and aluminum foil, packed either in plastic or glass containers, authorities said.
One man was injured slightly from the ingredients when he picked up one of the bombs, authorities said.
The students told authorities the bombs were meant to be harmless pranks, Gilston said.
"They didn't realise the potential for injurying someone or themselves when they made the bombs," he said. "Ignorance is youth."
Among those arrested were the captain of the football team and the president of the student council.
If convicted, they face fines of $2,000 and up to four years in prison.
